generated_by: scripts/audit_build.py (initial hand-verified pass, before first source sync)

chromium_version.note: Thorium has no pinned Chromium version file in its own meta-repo. Per Thorium's README, it is 'always built with the latest LTS version of Chromium', and win_scripts/upstream_version.py checks out the exact Chromium tag matching the current Thorium release at sync time. This field is filled in by `build.ps1 sync` from the checked-out src/chrome/VERSION file.

thorium_version.note: Thorium ships several prebuilt SIMD flavors (SSE2/SSE3/SSE4.1/AVX/AVX2/AVX-512) selected at setup time via win_scripts/setup.py flags, not a single 'version'. Windows binary releases are distributed from https://github.com/Alex313031/Thorium-Win (a separate, release-only repo).

compiler.toolchain: Clang/LLVM bundled via depot_tools (Chromium's pinned 'clang' package)
compiler.note: is_clang = true, use_lld = true in win_args.gn. Exact clang --version and LLVM revision are recorded by build.ps1 into build-manifest.json after `gclient runhooks` pulls the pinned toolchain -- must be new enough to recognize -march=znver5 (requires LLVM >= 16; LLVM 19+ recommended for the fullest Zen5 scheduler model). Verified at configure time by scripts/audit_build.py.

target_cpu.note: target_cpu=x64 is Chromium's ABI/pointer-width selector, unrelated to microarchitecture tuning. Microarchitecture targeting (-march=znver5) is controlled entirely by compiler cflags/ldflags, which Thorium hardcodes per SIMD flavor (see modified_files).

target_features.stock_avx512_feature_set_note: Deliberately the 'least common denominator' AVX-512 subset per compiler_opt.gni's own comment ('Only uses AVX-512 instructions common to all processors'). Zen5 additionally has AVX512VNNI, AVX512BITALG, AVX512VPOPCNTDQ, AVX512VBMI, AVX512VBMI2, AVX512IFMA, AVX512BF16, GFNI, VAES, VPCLMULQDQ, movdiri/movdir64b -- none of which stock Thorium enables.
target_features.zen5_profile_target_features: Not a hand-maintained flag list. gn/win_zen5_args.gn sets use_znver5=true (new arg added by patches/zen5), which replaces the entire manual -mavx512* cflag list with '-march=znver5 -mtune=znver5', letting Clang's znver5 CPU model select the complete correct ISA and scheduling itself, per the project's explicit design requirement.

pgo_enabled.mechanism: chrome_pgo_phase = 2 with pgo_data_path pointing at a downloaded .profdata file (win_scripts/setup.py calls tools/update_pgo_profiles.py --target=win64).
pgo_enabled.note: This PGO profile is Google's generic win64 Chrome profile, trained on generic hardware -- it is NOT Zen5-specific. Regenerating a Zen5-trained profile would require running Chromium's PGO instrumented-build + benchmark-training workflow locally (chrome_pgo_phase=1 instrumented build, run a representative workload, merge .profraw -> .profdata). This is a real, expensive undertaking; tracked as an unresolved question below and left as an opt-in, separate step (not part of the default zen5 profile) rather than silently skipped.

lto_enabled.mechanism: use_thin_lto = true, thin_lto_enable_optimizations = true (ThinLTO, not full/monolithic LTO).

avx512_enabled.enabled_by: other/AVX512/win_AVX512_args.gn (a distinct args.gn flavor, not a command-line flag to build_win.sh)
propagation_confirmed_in_meta_repo: src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn (cflags/ldflags, x64 Windows AND x64 Linux/Mac branches)
src/build/config/win/BUILD.gn (cflags, and a second ldflags block gating ThinLTO backend -march for release/non-component builds)
src/v8/BUILD.gn (separate cflags application for V8's own compile targets, Windows AND non-Windows branches)
src/chrome/installer/linux/BUILD.gn (package name suffix only -- '_AVX512'; irrelevant to Windows)
avx512_enabled.propagation_NOT_found_in_meta_repo: Chromium's own third-party SIMD libraries (highway, dav1d, libjpeg-turbo, libvpx/libaom, zlib, skia opts, etc.) are NOT touched by Thorium's use_avx512 flag anywhere in this meta-repo. This strongly suggests those libraries keep Chromium's stock behavior: compile multiple SIMD variants and pick one via CPU-feature runtime dispatch (cpu-features / base::CPU checks), independent of the use_avx512 GN arg. This must be re-verified once the real Chromium source tree exists (scripts/audit_build.py's 'source-tree' pass) -- Thorium's own meta-repo only contains files Thorium itself modifies, not the full Chromium tree, so this cannot be fully confirmed from the meta-repo alone.
avx512_enabled.root_cause_of_generic_avx512: src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn and src/build/config/win/BUILD.gn hardcode `-mllvm:-march=skylake-avx512` (Windows) / `-Wl,-mllvm,-march=skylake-avx512` (Linux/Mac) as the ThinLTO backend codegen/scheduling target whenever use_avx512=true, regardless of host CPU vendor. This is the exact 'generic AVX-512 treated as final target' problem described in the task.

B_already_cpu_dispatched_leave_alone: third_party/highway (Google Highway) -- runtime dispatch, compiles multiple targets
third_party/dav1d -- runtime dispatch via its own cpu.c detection
third_party/zlib -- runtime dispatch for its SIMD paths

NOTE: presence/exact list to be confirmed by scripts/audit_build.py once real Chromium source exists; classification here is based on documented Chromium upstream architecture, not yet re-verified against this checkout.
C_must_stay_generic: NaCl / cross-compilation toolchains (not used on this single-machine Windows target; not built)

build/toolchain/* GN toolchain definitions for non-host toolchains (e.g. any 32-bit or ARM helper binaries produced during the build, such as the x86 or WOA subprocess helpers, if any) -- must not receive znver5 flags
D_third_party_special_handling: other/AVX2/third_party/opus -- Thorium's own AVX2-tuned Opus build files, reused verbatim for the AVX-512 flavor via win_scripts/setup.py's copy_avx512(). Left untouched by the zen5 patches; still copied in by build.ps1 configure.
E_unknown_pending_real_source: Everything not explicitly listed above -- the meta-repo does not contain the full Chromium tree, so a full A/B/C/D classification of every third_party target requires re-running scripts/audit_build.py's source-tree pass after `build.ps1 sync`.

unresolved_questions: Exact bundled clang/LLVM version is not yet known (depends on Chromium revision at sync time); must be checked for znver5 recognition before first zen5 build (build.ps1 configure fails loudly if not recognized).
Whether Chromium's third-party SIMD libraries have any additional AVX-512 build-time (not runtime-dispatch) specialization worth pinning to znver5 -- requires the real source tree.

Whether to attempt a Zen5-trained PGO profile (expensive: instrumented build + representative workload + profile merge) instead of Google's generic win64 profile. Left as an explicit opt-in ('build.ps1 build -TrainPgo') rather than default.
infra/upgrader submodule points at a third-party fork (hezhizheng/thorium-win-upgrade), not an Alex313031 repo -- update.ps1 does not depend on it; noted for awareness only.

Thorium-Win (github.com/Alex313031/Thorium-Win) appears to be a release-binary distribution repo rather than an alternate source tree; assumed so here. If wrong, update.ps1's upstream-check step should also poll it.
